Sunni beliefs: Allah, angels (malaikah), books (kutub), prophets (rasul), Last Day, predestination (al-qadr).
Shia beliefs: Tawhid, Adalat (justice), Nubuwwah (prophethood), Imamah (Imams), Mi'ad (resurrection).
Prophethood; 25 prophets named in Qur'an including Adam, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, ending with Muhammad as Seal of Prophets.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Islam: Beliefs & Teachings — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Islam: Beliefs & Teachings brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Islam: Beliefs & Teachings.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many surahs are in the Qur'an?

options: Pilgrimage
Oneness of God
Charity
Prayer
The Shahada is the requirement to pray five times a day.
The Islamic declaration of faith: 'There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the messenger of Allah' — affirming monotheism and Muhammad's prophethood.
The Shahada is the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Sunni and Shia Islam?
options: Sunnis and Shias believe in different gods.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
They split over who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad: Sunnis accepted Abu Bakr and elected caliphs; Shias believed leadership should follow Muhammad's bloodline through Ali.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.

mcqs.q: How do Muslims believe the Quran was revealed?
options: The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
The Shahada is the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca.
Muhammad wrote the Quran based on his own teachings.
Through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) to Muhammad over 23 years; Muslims believe it is the literal word of God, not Muhammad's own words.
